scenario: Roll back live v0.1.5 (schema 0029) to v0.1.4 (schema 0029).

decision.note: v0.1.5 ships no migration, so the rollback target runs the same 0029 schema and the planner resolves to redeploy_without_database_restore. No database restore and no post-backup data loss are involved — materially safer than the v0.1.4 rollback, which crossed 0029 to 0028 and required a restore.

recovery_point.note: Captured as a precaution before promotion. Because the rollback needs no restore, this recovery point is not on the rollback path; it exists so a forward-fix decision has a verified point to fall back to if one is ever needed.

restore_verification_reference.note: Decrypted, restored into an isolated database, and application-verified during this rehearsal.

rpo_boundary: None for this rollback: the target release runs the same 0029 schema, so redeploying v0.1.4 components discards no data. A restore would only enter the picture if an unrelated failure required returning to an earlier schema.

forward_release_backup_verification.note: Proof that the live v0.1.5 (0029) schema backs up and restores cleanly with representative seeded data.

fail_closed_checks.reason: automatic/external agent rollout is not confirmed paused; the bad version could be reapplied

fail_closed_checks.case: recovery point schema does not match the rollback target
fail_closed_checks.input: 0029 recovery point offered for a 0028 target
fail_closed_checks.reason: backup schema revision does not match the target server schema; in-place Alembic downgrade is unsupported

environment.note: Rehearsal performed against a disposable PostgreSQL instance seeded with the representative dataset from server/tests/test_backup_restore.py, the same harness and dataset shape used for the v0.1.2, v0.1.3, and v0.1.4 release evidence. These are drill artifacts proving the procedure, not a production recovery point, and contain no production data. The rehearsal passphrase is operator-held and is not published with this evidence.
